title: Summary, review and chapter test
competency: Review the unit and take the timed chapter test.

keywords.def: Motion along a curved path in a plane, described with two coordinates.

en.text: Projectiles keep a constant horizontal velocity while falling with acceleration g. Rotating bodies are described by θ, ω and α, linked to linear motion by s = rθ, v = ωr and a = rα; torque τ = rF sinθ causes angular acceleration τ = Iα. Planets obey Kepler's laws because the Sun's gravity F = Gm₁m₂/r² supplies their centripetal force.

am.text: ተወንጫፊዎች ቋሚ አግድም ፍጥነት አላቸው። መዞር በ θ፣ ω፣ α ይገለጻል፤ τ = Iα። ፕላኔቶች የኬፕለርን ሕጎች ይከተላሉ፤ ምክንያቱም የፀሐይ ስበት ወደ መሀል የሚስብ ኃይል ነው።

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: Projectile: horizontal velocity constant, vertical acceleration g. Both motions share the same time.
Rotation: s = rθ, v = ωr, a = rα. Every particle has the same Δθ, ω and α.
Torque τ = rF sinθ; moment of inertia I = Σmr²; τ_net = Iα.
Kepler: ellipses, equal areas, T²/R³ = K.
Newton: F = Gm₁m₂/r², always attractive. The Sun's gravity is the planets' centripetal force.

screens.title: Key word
defs: Motion along a curved path in a plane, described with two coordinates.

screens.title: Match each formula to its idea
screens.why:
R = v₀² sin2θ/g: range of a projectile.
v = ωr: tangential speed of a turning point.
τ = Iα: Newton's second law for rotation.
T²/R³ = K: Kepler's third law.
F = Gm₁m₂/r²: universal gravitation.
screens.clue: Look at the letters: θ for angles, G for gravitation.
screens.text: Unit 2 review: match each formula to the idea it describes.

screens.ask: Components of velocity: a football is kicked at 20 m/s at 30°. Its horizontal velocity is ≈ ___ m/s (1 decimal place)
screens.why:
Formula: vₓ = v₀cosθ.
Substitute: vₓ = 20 × cos30° = 20 × 0.866.
Result: vₓ ≈ 17.3 m/s.
(The vertical part is v₀sinθ = 20 × 0.5 = 10 m/s.)
Trap: using sin gives 10 m/s, the vertical part.
screens.clue: Use cos for the horizontal part.

screens.ask: Braking wheel: α = −5.60 rad/s². In 4.20 s it turns 62.4 rad. Its final angular speed is ≈ ___ rad/s (1 decimal place)
screens.why:
Use Δθ = ω_f t − ½αt² (no ω₀ needed).
Rearrange: ω_f = Δθ/t + ½αt.
Substitute: ω_f = 62.4 ÷ 4.20 + ½ × (−5.60) × 4.20.
ω_f = 14.86 − 11.76 = 3.10 rad/s.
Check: ω₀ = 3.10 + 5.60 × 4.20 = 26.6 rad/s, and (26.6 + 3.1)/2 × 4.2 ≈ 62.4 rad ✓
screens.clue: Find ω₀ first, or use Δθ = ω_f t − ½αt².

items.ask: End of unit Q1 a, time of flight: a ball is thrown horizontally from the top of a 45 m building. It reaches the ground after ≈ ___ s (2 decimal places)
items.why:
Formula: t = √(2h/g).
Substitute: t = √(2 × 45 ÷ 9.8) = √9.18.
Result: t ≈ 3.03 s.
The launch speed does not change the fall time.

items.ask: End of unit Q1 b, horizontal distance: same ball, launched at 20 m/s (t = 3.03 s). It lands ≈ ___ m from the foot of the building (1 decimal place)
items.why:
Formula: Δx = v₀t.
Substitute: Δx = 20 m/s × 3.03 s.
Result: Δx ≈ 60.6 m.

items.ask: End of unit Q2 b, time of flight: a football is kicked at 20 m/s at 30° (g = 9.8 m/s²). Time of flight ≈ ___ s (2 decimal places)
items.why:
Formula: T = 2v₀sinθ/g.
v₀sinθ = 20 × 0.5 = 10 m/s.
T = 2 × 10 ÷ 9.8.
Result: T ≈ 2.04 s.

items.ask: End of unit Q2 c, range: same kick (20 m/s at 30°, g = 9.8 m/s²). Range ≈ ___ m (1 decimal place)
items.why:
Formula: R = v₀² sin2θ/g.
sin60° = 0.866.
R = 400 × 0.866 ÷ 9.8.
Result: R ≈ 35.3 m.
Check: vₓT = 17.32 × 2.04 ≈ 35.3 m ✓

items.ask: End of unit Q2 d, position in flight: same kick. Horizontal displacement at t = 1.5 s ≈ ___ m (1 decimal place)
items.why:
Formula: x = vₓt.
vₓ = 20cos30° = 17.32 m/s.
x = 17.32 × 1.5 ≈ 26.0 m.
1.5 s < 2.04 s, so the ball is still in the air.

items.ask: End of unit Q4, launch speed from landing point: a volcanic bomb leaves the vent at 35°; it lands 9.40 km away and 3.30 km lower. Launch speed ≈ ___ m/s (nearest whole number)
items.why:
Horizontal: v₀cos35° t = 9400, so v₀t = 9400 ÷ 0.819 = 11 475 m.
Vertical (up +): −3300 = v₀t sin35° − 4.9t² = 6582 − 4.9t².
4.9t² = 9882, so t² = 2017 and t ≈ 44.9 s.
v₀ = 11 475 ÷ 44.9 ≈ 256 m/s.
Trap: landing lower means Δy is negative.
items.clue: Write x and y equations; eliminate v₀t.

items.text: End of unit Q5, height on a wall: a firefighter at distance d aims water at angle θᵢ with speed vᵢ. It hits the building at height h =
items.why:
Horizontal: d = vᵢcosθᵢ t, so t = d/(vᵢcosθᵢ).
Vertical: h = vᵢsinθᵢ t − ½gt².
Substitute t: h = d tanθᵢ − gd²/(2vᵢ² cos²θᵢ).
Trap: a + sign would mean gravity pushes the water up.
items.clue: Find t from the horizontal motion.

items.ask: End of unit Q6, tip speed of a fan: 1200 rev/min, blade tip 0.15 m from the axis. Speed ≈ ___ m/s (1 decimal place)
items.why:
Convert: 1200 rev/min ÷ 60 = 20 rev/s.
ω = 20 × 2π = 125.7 rad/s.
v = ωr = 125.7 × 0.15.
Result: v ≈ 18.8 m/s.
items.clue: Change to rev/s, then multiply by the circumference.

items.ask: End of unit Q7, braking wheels: a car at 80 km/h with 40 cm wheels stops within 30 revolutions. |α| ≈ ___ rad/s² (2 decimal places)
items.why:
Convert: 80 km/h = 22.2 m/s; ω₀ = v/r = 22.2 ÷ 0.40 = 55.6 rad/s.
Convert: Δθ = 30 × 2π = 188.5 rad.
Use ω_f² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ with ω_f = 0.
α = −55.6² ÷ (2 × 188.5) = −3086 ÷ 377 = −8.19 rad/s².
So |α| ≈ 8.19 rad/s².

items.ask: End of unit Q8, angle turned: a grindstone belt turns at 40 rad/s. In one minute it turns ___ rad
items.why:
Constant ω: Δθ = ωt.
Δθ = 40 rad/s × 60 s.
Result: 2400 rad (≈ 382 rev).

items.ask: End of unit Q9, distance rolled: a wheel of radius 0.50 m makes 320 rotations. She travels ≈ ___ m (nearest metre)
items.why:
One turn rolls a distance 2πr = 2π × 0.50 = 3.14 m.
320 turns: 320 × 3.14 m.
Result: ≈ 1005 m.

items.text: Equilibrium is the state of an object when
opts: A. the net force acting on it is constant.
B. the object has a constant linear acceleration.
C. the net force and net torque are both zero.
D. the object has constant angular acceleration.
items.ans: C. the net force and net torque are both zero.
items.why:
First condition: ΣF = 0, so no linear acceleration.
Second condition: Στ = 0, so no angular acceleration.
Equilibrium needs both: answer C.
A: a constant non-zero net force still accelerates the object.
B and D describe accelerating objects, so they are not in equilibrium.

items.text: The fulcrum of a uniform 20 kg seesaw that is 4.0 m long is located 2.5 m from one end. A 30 kg child sits on the long end. The weight of a person sitting on the other end in order to balance the seesaw is (g = 10 m/s²)
items.why:
Arms: long side 2.5 m, short side 4.0 − 2.5 = 1.5 m.
The seesaw's weight (200 N) acts at its centre: 2.5 − 2.0 = 0.5 m on the long side.
Long-side torque: 300 N × 2.5 m + 200 N × 0.5 m = 750 + 100 = 850 N m.
Balance: W × 1.5 m = 850 N m, so W ≈ 567 N.
Trap: 750 N ignores the seesaw's own weight; 850 N is a torque, not a force.

items.text: For a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis,
opts: A. a point closer to the axis has smaller linear speed than a point farther from the axis.
B. a point closer to the axis has greater linear speed than a point farther from the axis.
C. for the same time interval, a point closer to the axis and a point farther from the axis travel the same linear distance.
D. for the same time interval, a point closer to the axis turns through a smaller angle than a point farther from the axis.
items.ans: A. a point closer to the axis has smaller linear speed than a point farther from the axis.
items.why:
All points of a rigid body have the same θ and ω.
Linear speed v = ωr grows with r.
So a point nearer the axis is slower: answer A.
B reverses v = ωr; C is wrong because s = rθ depends on r.
D is wrong: all points turn through the same angle.

items.text: A disk of radius 0.10 m and mass 0.1 kg is set into motion by a tangential force of 2.0 N applied at the edge of the disk. If the angular acceleration of the disk is 400 rad/s², the torque and angular velocity at 2.0 s are, respectively (the disk starts from rest)
items.why:
Torque of a tangential force: τ = Fr = 2.0 × 0.10 = 0.20 N m.
Check: I = ½mr² = ½ × 0.1 × 0.10² = 5 × 10⁻⁴ kg m²; α = τ/I = 400 rad/s² ✓
From rest: ω = αt = 400 × 2.0 = 800 rad/s.
Answer: D. Trap: A uses t = 1 s.

items.text: Choose a correct statement about centripetal force and centripetal acceleration.
opts: A. Centripetal force on an object moving in a circular path is perpendicular to the radius of the path.
B. Centripetal force on an object moving in a circular path tends to pull the object outward from the path.
C. For an object moving in a circular path, its centripetal force and centripetal acceleration are parallel and directed toward the center of the path.
D. Centripetal acceleration and centripetal force are constant in direction, but vary in magnitude.
items.ans: C. For an object moving in a circular path, its centripetal force and centripetal acceleration are parallel and directed toward the center of the path.
items.why:
Centripetal acceleration a_c = v²/r points to the centre.
Newton's second law: F_c = ma_c, so the force points the same way.
Both lie along the radius toward the centre: answer C.
A is wrong: they are along the radius (perpendicular to the velocity).
B is wrong (outward); D is wrong: the direction keeps changing.

items.text: According to Newton's law of Universal Gravitation,
opts: A. the period of a satellite orbiting the Earth in a circular orbit increases as the radius of its orbit increases.
B. the gravitational attraction between two objects is directly proportional to the square of the distance between them.
C. the speed of a satellite moving around the Earth in a circular orbit depends on the mass of the satellite.
D. for two interacting objects, the gravitational force exerted on a light object is less than the force on the heavy one.
items.ans: A. the period of a satellite orbiting the Earth in a circular orbit increases as the radius of its orbit increases.
items.why:
Gravity is the centripetal force: GMm/r² = mv²/r, so v = √(GM/r).
Period: T = 2πr/v = 2π√(r³/GM), so T grows with r: answer A.
B is wrong: F ∝ 1/r², not r².
C is wrong: v does not contain the satellite's mass m.
D is wrong: by Newton's third law both forces are equal.

items.text: A wheel rotating at angular speed of 20 rev/s is brought to rest after 40 rev under a constant angular acceleration. The angular acceleration of a point on the wheel is
items.why:
Given ω₀ = 20 rev/s, ω = 0, Δθ = 40 rev; no time is given.
Use ω² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ: 0 = 20² + 2α × 40.
80α = −400, so α = −5 rev/s² (slowing down).
Answer D. Trap: C has the right size but the wrong sign.

items.text: Which of the following is true about satellite motion?
opts: A. For equal orbital radius, a satellite moving around the Earth has smaller speed than a satellite moving about the Moon.
B. A satellite closer to the Earth is faster than a satellite farther from the Earth.
C. A satellite closer to the Earth takes longer time to complete one revolution than a satellite farther from the Earth.
D. For two satellites moving around the Earth at equal orbital radius, a heavier satellite has larger speed than a lighter one.
items.ans: B. A satellite closer to the Earth is faster than a satellite farther from the Earth.
items.why:
Orbit: v = √(GM/r), so smaller r gives larger v: answer B.
A is wrong: Earth's M is larger, so its satellite is faster at the same r.
C is wrong: T = 2π√(r³/GM) is shorter for smaller r.
D is wrong: v does not depend on the satellite's mass.

items.text: A torque τ rotates an object of mass m and moment of inertia I through an angle θ. The work done on the object by the torque is
items.why:
Linear work: W = Fs.
For a tangential force at radius r: s = rθ.
W = F × rθ = (Fr)θ = τθ (θ in radians): answer A.
Iθ and mθ do not have units of energy; τd mixes rotation with a straight distance.

items.text: A 30 kg rigid object has a moment of inertia 45 kg·m² about its center of mass. What is the object's moment of inertia when it rotates through an axis 2 m away and parallel to the axis through its center of mass?
items.why:
Parallel-axis theorem: I = I_cm + Md².
Md² = 30 kg × (2 m)² = 120 kg m².
I = 45 + 120 = 165 kg m²: answer B.
Trap: D uses d instead of d² (45 + 60 = 105).

test.ask: Free fall: a stone falls from rest for 3 s (g = 10 m/s²). It falls ___ m
test.why:
From rest: h = ½gt².
h = ½ × 10 × 3² = 5 × 9.
Result: 45 m.

test.text: Projectile motion: the horizontal velocity of a projectile
test.why:
No horizontal force acts (no air resistance).
So the horizontal acceleration is zero.
The horizontal velocity stays constant.
Trap: it is v_y, not vₓ, that is zero at the top.

test.ask: Arc length: a wheel of radius 0.5 m turns through 10 rad. A rim point moves ___ m
test.why:
Formula: s = rθ (θ in radians).
s = 0.5 × 10.
Result: 5 m.

test.ask: Torque and angular acceleration: a torque of 20 N m acts on I = 5 kg m². α = ___ rad/s²
test.why:
Formula: α = τ/I.
α = 20 ÷ 5.
Result: 4 rad/s².

test.ask: Kepler's third law: a satellite's orbit radius is 9 times another's around the same planet. Its period is ___ times longer

notes.text: End of unit Q1 gives no launch speed, so (b) and (c) have no number. The lesson adds v₀ = 20 m/s (x = 60.6 m; v = 35.8 m/s at 56.0° below horizontal).
Unit summary: Δy = v₀sinθ t + ½gt² and v_y = v₀sinθ + gt only work with g = −9.8 m/s².
The chapter test mixes section-test items with past national-exam (EUEE 2013, ESSLCE 2014–2015) questions; items whose key we dispute are left out.
